questions.prompt: The general, having destroyed the enemy camp, wept for the slain soldiers.
questions.answer: Dux, castrīs hostium dēlētīs, mīlitēs occīsōs flēvit.

questions.prompt: We had filled the deep valleys with the lament of the mourners.
questions.answer: Vallēs profundās plangōre lūgentium complēverāmus.

questions.prompt: Old age destroyed his strength, and he grieved that he lacked his former vigor.
questions.answer: Senectūs vīrēs eius abolēvit, et doluit sē prīstinō rōbore caruisse.

questions.prompt: The storm set the waves in motion and frightened the fishermen on the shore.
questions.answer: Tempestās flūctūs cīvit et piscātōrēs in lītore terruit.

questions.prompt: The strong walls kept the enemy away from the sleeping city.
questions.answer: Validī mūrī hostem ab urbe dormiente arcuērunt.

questions.prompt: The prudent consul held the raging crowd in check with a few words.
questions.answer: Cōnsul prūdēns turbam saevientem paucīs verbīs coercuit.

questions.prompt: For many years the athletes had practiced their bodies in the sacred meadow.
questions.answer: Multōs annōs athlētae corpora in prātō sacrō exercuerant.

questions.prompt: Having trained their minds daily, the students earned great praise.
questions.answer: Discipulī, animīs cotīdiē exercitīs, magnam laudem meruērunt.

questions.prompt: The merchant, who owed much money, offered his house as a pledge.
questions.answer: Mercātor, quī multam pecūniam dēbēbat, domum suam pignorī praebuit.

questions.prompt: The soldiers who had earned rewards held the highest honors.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs quī praemia meruerant summōs honōrēs habuērunt.

questions.prompt: The host offered myrrh and rare ointments to his weary guests.
questions.answer: Hospes murram et rāra unguenta fessīs hospitibus praebuit.

questions.prompt: We ought to advise our friends, although the truth often brings pain.
questions.answer: Amīcōs monēre dēbēmus, quamquam vēritās saepe dolōrem affert.

questions.prompt: The seer had warned the king that the omens were frightening the people.
questions.answer: Vātēs rēgem monuerat ōmina populum terrēre.

questions.prompt: The gentle song pleased the goddess, and the whole grove fell silent.
questions.answer: Carmen lēne deae placuit, et tōtum nemus tacuit.

questions.prompt: The citizens obeyed the laws, because they feared the harsh magistrate.
questions.answer: Cīvēs lēgibus pāruērunt, quod magistrātum sevērum verēbantur.

questions.prompt: The wounded warrior lay in the field and grieved for his lost companions.
questions.answer: Vulnerātus bellātor in campō iacuit et āmissōs comitēs doluit.

questions.prompt: The hearth was warm, although the traveler lacked both food and wine.
questions.answer: Focus calēbat, quamquam viātor et cibō et vīnō carēbat.

questions.prompt: The long siege harmed the citizens, yet their courage remained strong.
questions.answer: Longa obsidiō cīvibus nocuit, sed eōrum virtūs valuit.

questions.prompt: The old man, who was without hope, grieved and lay awake through the night.
questions.answer: Senex, quī spē carēbat, doluit et per noctem vigil iacuit.

questions.prompt: The lofty tower stood forth above the walls and frightened the approaching foe.
questions.answer: Turris alta suprā mūrōs ēminuit et hostem appropinquantem terruit.

questions.prompt: The whole army shuddered when the trumpet set their hearts in motion.
questions.answer: Tōtus exercitus horruit, cum tuba animōs cīvit.

questions.prompt: In spring the meadows bloomed, and the shepherd wept for joy.
questions.answer: Vēre prāta flōruērunt, et pāstor gaudiō flēvit.
